# <span id="Introduction" class="mw-headline">Introduction</span>

This is a sound card HAT designed for Raspberry Pi, has low power consumption, supports stereo encoding/decoding, features high-quality playing/recording, what's more, it can directly drive speakers to play music.

## <span id="Features" class="mw-headline">Features</span>

-   Standard Raspberry Pi 40PIN GPIO extension header, supports Raspberry Pi series boards.
-   Integrates WM8960 low power stereo CODEC, communicates via I2S interface.
-   Integrates dual high-quality MEMS silicon Mic, supports left & right double channels recording nice sound quality.
-   Onboard standard 3.5mm earphone jack, play music via external earphones.
-   Onboard dual-channel speaker interface, directly drives speakers.
-   Supports sound effects such as stereo, 3D surroundings, etc.

## <span id="Specifications" class="mw-headline">Specifications</span>

-   CODEC: WM8960
-   Power supply: 5V
-   Logic voltage: 3.3V
-   Control interface: I2C
-   Audio interface: I2S
-   DAC signal-noise ratio: 98dB
-   ADC signal-noise ratio: 94dB
-   Earphone driver: 40mW (16Ω@3.3V)
-   Speaker driver: 1W per channel (8Ω BTL)

## <span id="Dimension" class="mw-headline">Dimension</span>

<a href="/wiki/File:WM8960-Audio-HAT-size.jpg" class="image"><img src="/w/upload/thumb/5/5a/WM8960-Audio-HAT-size.jpg/500px-WM8960-Audio-HAT-size.jpg" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="/w/upload/thumb/5/5a/WM8960-Audio-HAT-size.jpg/750px-WM8960-Audio-HAT-size.jpg 1.5x, /w/upload/5/5a/WM8960-Audio-HAT-size.jpg 2x" width="500" height="249" alt="WM8960-Audio-HAT-size.jpg" /></a>

## <span id="Hardware_Resource" class="mw-headline">Hardware Resource</span>

<a href="/wiki/File:WM8960_Audio_HAT.png" class="image"><img src="/w/upload/5/54/WM8960_Audio_HAT.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="500" height="249" alt="WM8960 Audio HAT.png" /></a>  
LP and LN correspond to the positive and negative poles of the left speaker respectively; RP and RN correspond to the positive and negative poles of the right speaker respectively.  

|                 |                         |                                 |
|-----------------|-------------------------|---------------------------------|
| Functional Pins | Raspberry Pi Pins (BCM) | Description                     |
| 5V              | 5V                      | Power positive (5V power input) |
| GND             | GND                     | Power Ground                    |
| SDA             | P2/SDA                  | I2C data input                  |
| SCL             | P3/SCL                  | I2C clock Input                 |
| CLK             | P18                     | I2S bit clock input             |
| LRCLK           | P19                     | I2S frame clock input           |
| DAC             | P21                     | I2S serial data output          |
| ADC             | P20                     | I2S serial data input           |
| BUTTON          | P17                     | Custom buttons                  |

# <span id="Raspberry_Pi_User_Guide" class="mw-headline">Raspberry Pi User Guide</span>

The guides can only be used with Raspberry Pi OS (Raspbian).

## <span id="Install_Driver" class="mw-headline">Install Driver</span>

Clone driver:

    git clone https://github.com/waveshare/WM8960-Audio-HAT

Install WM8960 driver:  

    cd WM8960-Audio-HAT
    sudo chmod +x install.sh
    sudo ./install.sh 
    sudo reboot

Check if the driver is installed.  

    sudo dkms status

    pi@raspberrypi:~ $ sudo dkms status 
    wm8960-soundcard, 1.0, 4.19.58-v7l+, armv7l: installed

  
Note: If the WM8960 Audio HAT has a noise problem, please reinstall the driver and test it again.  
In addition, you can use this pre-configured image os for a try.

    https://drive.google.com/file/d/1D1WE30Ijsxu3f4NpLtQKYrX_D4gkEOFT/view?usp=drive_link 

If the 3.5mm jack has no audio output, please run the following command to restart the service.

    sudo systemctl restart wm8960-soundcard.service

## <span id="Check_the_Soundcard" class="mw-headline">Check the Soundcard</span>

-   Test playing：aplay -l

<!-- -->

    pi@raspberrypi:~ $ aplay -l
    **** List of PLAYBACK Hardware Devices ****
    card 0: wm8960soundcard [wm8960-soundcard], device 0: bcm2835-i2s-wm8960-hifi wm8960-hifi-0 []
      Subdevices: 1/1
      Subdevice #0: subdevice #0

-   Test recording：arecord -l

<!-- -->

    pi@raspberrypi:~ $ arecord -l
    **** List of CAPTURE Hardware Devices ****
    card 0: wm8960soundcard [wm8960-soundcard], device 0: bcm2835-i2s-wm8960-hifi wm8960-hifi-0 []
      Subdevices: 1/1
      Subdevice #0: subdevice #0

## <span id="Test_record/play"></span><span id="Test_record.2Fplay" class="mw-headline">Test record/play</span>

### <span id="Record_&_Play"></span><span id="Record_.26_Play" class="mw-headline">Record & Play</span>

    sudo arecord -f cd -Dhw:0 | aplay -Dhw:0

After running the command, you can hear the sound recorded by mic from earphones or speakers. Note that the speaker should be away from the mic to void from noise.  

### <span id="Record" class="mw-headline">Record</span>

    sudo arecord -D hw:0,0 -f S32_LE -r 16000 -c 2 test.wav

test.wav is the file name outputed.  

### <span id="Play" class="mw-headline">Play</span>

    sudo aplay -Dhw:0 test.wav

Play the audio.  

### <span id="Adjust_the_volume" class="mw-headline">Adjust the volume</span>

The default volume is small, and you can install the alsamixer to adjust it.  

    sudo alsamixer

If WM8960 is not the default sound card, you should press F6 to choose an audio device.  
<a href="/wiki/File:Wm8960_audio_hat_alsamixer.png" class="image"><img src="/w/upload/thumb/4/47/Wm8960_audio_hat_alsamixer.png/500px-Wm8960_audio_hat_alsamixer.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="/w/upload/4/47/Wm8960_audio_hat_alsamixer.png 1.5x" width="500" height="393" alt="Wm8960 audio hat alsamixer.png" /></a>  
In fact, there are many options on the right that can be adjusted.

### <span id="mpg123_palyer" class="mw-headline">mpg123 palyer</span>

aplay command can only support wav files, if you want to play MP3 file, you can install the mpg123 tool:  

    sudo apt-get install mpg123 
    sudo mpg123 music.mp3

You can replace the music.mp3 with the actual file name.  

### <span id="smplayer_for_GUI_controlling" class="mw-headline">smplayer for GUI controlling</span>

Note that this software can only work for:

    sudo apt-get install smplayer

Right-click and set the wm8960-soundcard as the default device.  
<a href="/wiki/File:Wm8960_audio_hat_smplayer.png" class="image"><img src="/w/upload/5/52/Wm8960_audio_hat_smplayer.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="500" height="285" alt="Wm8960 audio hat smplayer.png" /></a>  
Open the smplayer software in Menu, choose an audio file and play.  
<a href="/wiki/File:Wm8960_audio_hat_smplayer2.png" class="image"><img src="/w/upload/e/e9/Wm8960_audio_hat_smplayer2.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="500" height="602" alt="Wm8960 audio hat smplayer2.png" /></a>  
<a href="/wiki/File:Wm8960_audio_hat_smplayer3.png" class="image"><img src="/w/upload/thumb/f/fa/Wm8960_audio_hat_smplayer3.png/500px-Wm8960_audio_hat_smplayer3.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" srcset="/w/upload/f/fa/Wm8960_audio_hat_smplayer3.png 1.5x" width="500" height="395" alt="Wm8960 audio hat smplayer3.png" /></a>  

## <span id="Examples" class="mw-headline">Examples</span>

We provide examples for testing.  

-   Install ibraries

<!-- -->

    sudo apt-get install libasound2-dev
    git clone https://github.com/larsimmisch/pyalsaaudio
    cd pyalsaaudio
    sudo python3 setup.py build
    sudo python3 setup.py install

-   Download examples:

<!-- -->

    wget https://files.waveshare.com/upload/1/19/WM8960_Audio_HAT_Code.tar.gz
    tar zxvf WM8960_Audio_HAT_Code.tar.gz
    sudo chmod 777 -R WM8960_Audio_HAT_Code

-   Play:

<!-- -->

    sudo python playwav.py music.wav

-   Record:

<!-- -->

    sudo python recordwav.py out.wav

## <span id="WM8960" class="mw-headline">WM8960</span>

Try printing to the position shown in the picture in U-boot, and press any key to switch to the device tree.  
<a href="/wiki/File:VisionFive013.jpg" class="image"><img src="/w/upload/c/c4/VisionFive013.jpg" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="581" height="253" alt="VisionFive013.jpg" /></a>  

Replace the command at startup with the following:  

    ext4load mmc 1:3 a0000000 /boot/uEnv.txt 
    env import a0000000 17c
    setenv fdtfile starfive/jh7110-visionfive-v2-wm8960.dtb 
    sysboot mmc 1:3 ext2 b0000000 /boot/extlinux/extlinux.conf

## <span id="202302_System,_Driver_Loading"></span><span id="202302_System.2C_Driver_Loading" class="mw-headline">202302 System, Driver Loading</span>

Boot and enter the system, and input the commands:

    nano /boot/uEnv.txt

Go to the system boot configuration file, comment out section 1, and add section 2:

    fdtfile=starfive/jh7110-visionfive-v2-wm8960.dtb

<a href="/wiki/File:202302_System_Loading01.png" class="image"><img src="/w/upload/5/59/202302_System_Loading01.png" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="546" height="273" alt="202302 System Loading01.png" /></a>  
Reboot.

## <span id="Start_to_Use" class="mw-headline">Start to Use</span>

Install alsa-utils  

    apt install alsa-utils

If the module is not connected at the beginning, you need to restart VisionFive2 to detect the audio device.  
Type aplay -l to list sound cards and digital audio devices.  
Pay attention to the position marked on the picture, which indicates the device number of the sound card and digital audio equipment, where card0 and device0 are the headphone jacks on the VisionFive2 board, card0 and device2 are the headphone jacks on the WM8960 module.  
<a href="/wiki/File:VisionFive290.jpg" class="image"><img src="/w/upload/a/a5/VisionFive290.jpg" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="799" height="189" alt="VisionFive290.jpg" /></a>  
Type arecord -l to list sound cards and recording devices.  
Pay attention to the position marked on the picture, which indicates the device number of the sound card and recording device, card0 and device1 are the two patch microphones on the WM8960 module.  
<a href="/wiki/File:VisionFive291.jpg" class="image"><img src="/w/upload/8/81/VisionFive291.jpg" decoding="async" loading="lazy" width="794" height="111" alt="VisionFive291.jpg" /></a>  
Input the command:  

    arecord -Dhw:0,1 -f S32_LE -r16000 -c2 -d 10 -t wav sound_32b_16k.wav

Start recording 10 seconds of 32-bit, 16kHz audio, and save it in the current directory, the file name is sound_32b_16k.wav.  
input the command:  

    aplay -Dhw:0,2 -f S32_LE -r16000 -t wav sound_32b_16k.wav

Use the WM8960 module onboard headphone interface to play audio.  
Note that the headphone jack on the VisionFive2 board only supports audio output in 16-bit audio format.  

# <span id="RDK_X3_Module_Usage" class="mw-headline">RDK X3 Module Usage</span>

## <span id="Recording_Playback_Function" class="mw-headline">Recording Playback Function</span>

If you are using the server image, please import the latest two audio packages to the system, if not please skip to the driver installation.

    wget https://files.waveshare.com/upload/3/39/Audio_Driver_HAT_V2.zip
    unzip Audio_Driver_HAT_V2.zip
    sudo dpkg -i *.deb
    sync
    sudo reboot

Install the driver:

    git clone [email protected]:HorizonRDK/hobot-audio.git
    cd hobot-audio
    sudo ./install.sh
    What type of audio board do you have?
    1. WM8960 Audio HAT
    2. Audio Driver HAT

Select "1".  
Run "sync && reboot" and reboot the development board. If the following device node appears under "/dev/snd", the adapter board is successfully installed.  

    root@ubuntu:~# ls /dev/snd/
    by-path  controlC0  pcmC0D0c  pcmC0D0p  pcmC0D1c  pcmC0D1p  timer

### <span id="Recording_Playback_Test" class="mw-headline">Recording Playback Test</span>

Channel 2 microphone recording:

    tinycap ./2chn_test.wav -D 0 -d 0 -c 2 -b 16 -r 48000 -p 512 -n 4 -t 5

Dual channel audio playback:

    tinyplay ./2chn_test.wav -D 0 -d 1

# <span id="FAQ" class="mw-headline">FAQ</span>

#### <a href="#accordion1" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: I want to install the WM8960_Audio_HAT on a Raspberry Pi Zero W. Used Bullseye 32-Bit Lite as OS, but it cannot work?</a>

 **Answer:**

The default setting missed several libraries.  
Please use this pre-configured image os for a try.

    https://drive.google.com/file/d/1D1WE30Ijsxu3f4NpLtQKYrX_D4gkEOFT/view?usp=drive_link 

{{{5}}}

  

#### <a href="#accordion2" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: The driver cannot be installed properly in the newest Raspberry Pi because of less kernel-header issue?</a>

 **Answer:**

Add the following line to the /boot/config.txt, reboot, and install the driver again for a try.

    arm_64bit=0

  

#### <a href="#accordion3" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: For systems with different kernels, how should I download the corresponding drivers?</a>

 **Answer:**

-   Check the kernel version first

<!-- -->

    uname --all

-   If the kernel version of your system is lower than 5.0 (that is, the Raspberry Pi system version is before 2020-05-27), please download the following driver:

<!-- -->

    git clone -b rpi-4.9.y https://github.com/waveshare/WM8960-Audio-HAT.git

-   If the kernel version is higher than 5.0, please download the following driver:

<!-- -->

    git clone https://github.com/waveshare/WM8960-Audio-HAT

【Note】Please do not run both of the above two commands!

{{{3}}}

{{{4}}}

{{{5}}}

  

#### <a href="#accordion4" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: Why could the speaker work but the earphones of WM8960 Audio HAT not work?</a>

 **Answer:**

Please run the following command to restart the sound card service and test it again.

    sudo systemctl restart wm8960-soundcard.service

{{{3}}}

{{{4}}}

{{{5}}}

  

#### <a href="#accordion5" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: How many sections are the headphone sockets?</a>

 **Answer:**

The headphone holder is a 4-segment national standard (also known as OMTP) headphone jack. If it is an American standard (also known as CTIA) headphone, there may be no sound from the microphone.

{{{5}}}

  

#### <a href="#accordion6" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: What's the frequency of the crystal on the board?</a>

 **Answer:**

24Mhz.

{{{5}}}

  

#### <a href="#accordion7" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: What's the power of the speaker?</a>

 **Answer:**

Both speakers are 8 ohm 5W.

{{{5}}}

  

#### <a href="#accordion8" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: Is it possible to play while recording?</a>

 **Answer:**

Yes, as detailed in the recording test section of the instructions.

{{{5}}}

  

#### <a href="#accordion9" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: WM8960 Audio HAT driver is installed, why can't the sound card be detected?</a>

 **Answer:**

1\. Check if the /boot/config.txt file has blocked the default audio of the Raspberry Pi.  
2. Pay attention to whether the driver version is used.  
3. Make sure that no errors are reported during the driver installation.  
4. Be sure to restart after installation.  

{{{5}}}

  

#### <a href="#accordion10" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: The WM8960-Audio-HAT does not work on kernel 6.1.21-v8+ (aarch64)?</a>

 **Answer:**

Please check the 64-bit OS and you need to install the driver twice if you get the kernel error.  
Add the following line to the config file, reboot, and install the driver again for a try.  

    arm_64bit=0

{{{5}}}

  

#### <a href="#accordion11" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: Can we use the mic functionality on this HAT module by putting the jack into the earphone port or by any other means?</a>

 **Answer:**

The WM8960 Audio HAT doesn't feature external MIC input pins even on the 3.5mm jack.

{{{5}}}

  

#### <a href="#accordion12" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: I installed the WM8960 Audio Hat according to the instructions on your website onto a new Raspberry Pi 5 8GM and got the following error after reboot (w/o any audio working): "overlay 'vc4-kms-v3d' is not supported on the 'bcm2712' platform" Can you help?</a>

 **Answer:**

Please flash the original bookworm OS again and install the driver with the attached script for a try. The script drive link:

    https://drive.google.com/file/d/1FHFUeeKJfOtTUBplh2MFb94kkeRkd7wK/view?usp=sharing

{{{5}}}

  

#### <a href="#accordion13" data-parent="#accordion" data-toggle="collapse">Question: Is there a way to uninstall the previous driver as I have installed and configured my bookwork already?</a>

 **Answer:**

If possible, please use the fresh SD card for testing with WM8960 Audio Hat Raspberry Pi 5.
